title: Chapter 141 — Installation Problems
intro: The dishwasher leaks. The range is not level. The fridge doors hit the cabinet.

sections.title: Common Install Failures by Category
sections.content:
Dishwashers: leaking from the supply line connection, not sitting level, door hitting adjacent cabinetry. Ranges: not level, gas connection leak, anti-tip bracket not installed. Refrigerators: door swing blocked by wall or cabinet, water line leaking at ice maker connection, unit not level causing door alignment issues. Washers: excessive vibration from unlevel floor or shipping bolts not removed, drain connection leaking.

Most of these are preventable with proper pre-sale measurement verification and competent installation.

sections.title: The 24-Hour Check
sections.content:
Ask the customer to check within 24 hours: is the unit level? Are all connections dry — no water on the floor? Do the doors open fully without hitting anything? Is it making any unusual noises?

A 24-hour catch is easy to fix. A 2-week catch often means water damage to floors or cabinets.

sections.title: Repair vs Return
sections.content:
When to send the crew back: loose connection, leveling issue, minor adjustment needed. When to replace: persistent leak after crew visit, damaged door or panel, unit not functioning. When to escalate to manufacturer: suspected product defect, repeated failures on the same model.

The customer should never feel like they are coordinating between your install team and the manufacturer. You are the single point of contact. You coordinate. They wait.
